question: Salem commissioned 98 MLD of sewage treatment capacity years before the 2019 action plan - why is the Thirumanimutharu still Priority I?
intro: The 2019 action plan's own admission: four STPs totalling 98 MLD were 'commissioned four years before' but idle because the sewer network reaching them was unfinished. Everything since is the story of that network.

primary.label: TNPCB stretch-wise monthly water-quality reports
primary.note: December 2023 is the last stretch-wise edition TNPCB has published. Every month of 2023 at the stretch station (Uthamasolapuram, 3022) was Class E - BOD 6.4 to 27 mg/L against the bathing target of 3.

actionPlan.label: TNPCB Action Plan on Rejuvenation of River Thirumanimutharu (Sept 2019)

baseline.banner: Tamil Nadu publishes no stretch-wise infrastructure progress report - Karnataka's stretches have NMCG monthly progress reports; here implementation status has to be reconstructed from NGT case records. That absence is itself a finding.
otherSources: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report, October 2025 (mirrored on this site): station 3022 max BOD 60 (2022-23 basis) rising to 120 (2024)
NGT (SZ) judgment in O.A. 51/2015, 27 July 2021 - STP inflow and house-connection counts
NGT (SZ) order in O.A. 96/2023, 11 January 2024 - 48 MLD treatment gap, environmental compensation
TN Environment Dept Policy Note 2025-26 - stretch still listed Priority I

regions.name: Salem City Municipal Corporation
regions.inBasinNote: 913,188 people; 100 MLD sewage generated; 8 mapped outfalls into the river (2019 plan, p.9).

categories.label: Public STPs & sewer network

actionPlan.summary: UGSS at Rs 149.39 crore feeding 4 STPs of 98 MLD (Vellakuttai 13, Anaimedu 6, Vandipettai 44, Mankuttai 35), completion December 2019 (Package-2 December 2020); 40,000 house connections by December 2019. The plan concedes the STPs were commissioned years earlier but idle for want of sewers - only 1.5-2 MLD was reaching Vellakuttai.

mpr.summary: Tracked only through NGT case records, not any progress report. July 2021: 17.6 of 98 MLD treated; 12,530 of 84,222 connections; Vandipettai zero of 36,983. January 2022: 23.5 MLD; deadlines re-set to April/August 2022. January 2024: the Joint Committee still found a 48 MLD treatment gap and named Salem's domestic sewage the river's major pollution factor. July 2026: a TNPCB official told Junior Vikatan the UGSS remains incomplete.

gaps: The plan's December 2019 deadline has slipped through at least four public re-targets (Jan 2022, Aug 2022, May 2023, and 'ongoing' in July 2026) - six and a half years and counting.
No public house-connection count exists after January 2022 (12,894 of 84,222).
A second-generation Rs 530 crore UGSS for uncovered areas was announced in December 2021; seven Salem sewer packages were placed under independent audit in July 2026 (TNCRUDP).
Water-quality outcome: all 12 months of 2023 were Class E at the stretch station; CPCB's 2024 maximum BOD was 120 mg/L - worse than the 60 that fixed its Priority-I class.

actionPlan.summary: 370 TPD generated; 7 GPS-mapped dumping points on the river; commitments: 100% segregation by 30.06.2019, 30 micro-composting centres by April 2019, 10 more by October 2019, on-site composting at 86 locations by April 2019.

mpr.summary: No public record found of any of the dated solid-waste commitments being completed, or of the 7 riverbank dumping points being cleared.
mpr.asOf: July 2026 (search of NGT records, policy notes, municipal publications)

actionPlan.summary: The action plan never mentions biomedical waste - the same systemic omission found in every Karnataka action plan on this atlas.
actionPlan.cite: Thirumanimutharu Action Plan (TNPCB, Sept 2019) - no mention

mpr.summary: Nothing to report against - the category was never planned.

regions.name: Salem dyeing & sago clusters (Erumapalaiyam, Karungalpatti and others)
regions.inBasinNote: 357 effluent-generating units in the four riverside taluks; ~62 sago and 100+ dyeing/bleaching units in the plan's own annexure; 277 units dismantled and 99 EB-disconnected by Feb 2019.

categories.label: Industrial effluent

actionPlan.summary: The action table's industrial row says 'No industrial discharge' and sets no time target; the conclusion separately binds TNPCB to ensure no untreated dyeing/bleaching discharge 'at any point of time'. All dyeing/bleaching units are claimed to be on ZLD.

mpr.summary: The record since contradicts the no-discharge claim: CPCB's October 2025 stretch description itself reads 'D/S of sago & textile dying industries'; an NGT complaint over named dyeing units (2023) led to a Joint Committee and Rs 4.70 crore in environmental compensation levied (Rs 1.46 crore collected, Jan 2024); a fish kill in January 2025 was attributed to dyeing/bleaching effluent; activists counted 80+ discharging units in July 2026.

gaps: No public register reconciles the 2019 'all units on ZLD' claim with the 2023-2026 discharge record.
The compensation ledger (Rs 4.70 crore levied vs 1.46 collected) has no published follow-up.

media.label: Junior Vikatan, 11 July 2026 - river running black; 80+ dyeing units counted; TNPCB cites incomplete UGSS

regions.name: Papparapatti Village Panchayat
regions.inBasinNote: 9,020 people, 0.72 MLD; the stretch's downstream end.

actionPlan.summary: Individual and community soak pits under MGNREGS 2019-21, target October 2019, 'after construction of soak pits no waste water will be disposed into the river'.

mpr.summary: No completion record found in any public source.
